newsitem.title: UK: Big N Irish unionist party to meet Catholic Church.
newsitem.headline: Big N Irish unionist party to meet Catholic Church.

text.p: Northern Ireland's main pro-British unionist party plans a landmark meeting with leaders of the Catholic Church in the province within weeks, a party official said on Sunday.

In another hopeful sign for the faltering peace process, leaders of a Protestant organisation said they were re-routing two parades later this month so that they do not pass through a Catholic enclave in Belfast.

Dermot Nesbit of the Ulster Unionist Party told BBC radio the unprecedented meeting with the Catholic churchmen would take place early next month, before the September 15 resumption of talks on Northern Ireland's future.
The BBC later reported that Archbishop Sean Brady, head of the Catholic Church in Ireland, would take part in the meeting.

The Ulster Unionists are agonising over whether to remain in the talks now that Sinn Fein, the political wing of the Irish Republican Army, has been invited to join them following an IRA cease-fire in its fight to end British rule over the province.
The party's principal Protestant rivals, the Democratic Unionists, have said they will not sit at the same table with Sinn Fein unless the IRA gives up its vast cache of weapons and explosives.

Nesbit, who is leading a consultation process to help the Ulster Unionist party make up its mind, said the meeting with the Catholics would be only one of a number of discussions with community groups.
He said it was "part of a genuine attempt to listen to community representatives on ways of moving forward".

Meanwhile, leaders of the City of Belfast Grand Black Chapter, a Protestant organisation, relieved fears of violence on the city's streets later this month when it said it had accepted official advice to route two marches away from the Lower Ormeau Road Catholic area.

In a statement, the organisation said: "As a gesture of Christian goodwill with malice to none, we have decided under regrettable duress to submit to police advice on our traditional parades for the current year."
The organisation's two parades, the first planned for next Sunday, are among the last of a series of Protestant marches which take place annually in the province.
While most parades pass off peacefully, there are always fears of violence at those which are routed through areas where Catholics live.
